prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a damaged shed or outbuilding. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When the main issue is a damaged shed or outbuilding, check first whether it is part of the insured property and whether any contents are claimed, because outbuildings can be covered differently from the main house and the contents drive the scope of assessment."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the damage looks storm-related, I should look for corroborating signs such as missing fixings, lifted felt, shifted panels or scattered debris, because isolated wear and tear is common on sheds and should not be treated as insured storm damage without evidence."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a shed is old or lightly built, I should expect pre-existing deterioration to be a major factor and separate that from the event damage, especially where rot, rust, split timber or perished roofing are obvious."},{"type":"preference","content":"When there is a side wall or roof collapse, I prefer to ask whether the structure was already leaning, weakened or overloaded, because that often determines whether simple repair is viable or whether the loss is effectively due to gradual failure."},{"type":"fact","content":"When escape of water is mentioned, I should check for stored tools, garden furniture or electrical items that may also be damaged, because hidden contents losses can exceed the structure repair cost on small outbuildings."},{"type":"observation","content":"When there is alleged theft from a shed, I should look for signs of forced entry, secure locks and whether high-value items were left in a vulnerable place, because shed theft claims often depend on the quality of the security evidence."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the shed is used as a workshop or hobby room, I should confirm the permitted use under the policy and note any change in occupancy or business use, because that can affect whether the outbuilding falls within delegated authority."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the damage is minor and localised, I prefer to consider a like-for-like repair or replacement of panels, doors or roofing sheets rather than full replacement, because that usually resolves the claim proportionately and quickly."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a garden outbuilding is close to a boundary or exposed to wind, I should check whether neighbouring structures, trees or fences caused the impact, because external objects often explain the pattern of damage better than the weather alone."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the claim includes removal of debris or making safe, I should capture that early, because damaged sheds can leave sharp timber, unstable roofs or exposed wiring and the immediate risk can be more urgent than the final repair decision."}]}
